sections.h2: How did the Town of Palm Tree come to exist?
sections.html:
Palm Tree became an Orange County town on January 1, 2019, and its borders match the village of Kiryas Joel exactly. Voters approved the split from the Town of Monroe in a referendum on November 7, 2017, and a 2018 state law moved the start date up by a year. In 2019 residents also chose a single consolidated town and village government that operates like a village (Wikipedia).

The footprint is 1.5 square miles, with only a small pond near the center counted as water. Packed into that space are roughly 22,540 people per square mile. The April 2020 head count found 32,954 residents, and the mid-2025 estimate of 47,147 is 43.1 percent above its 2020 base.

Deeds, tax maps and surveys from before 2019 may name Monroe or the village, while newer records name Palm Tree. Check that the deed, the tax bill and the survey all describe your lot the same way.

sections.h2: What does the Census show about housing in Palm Tree?
sections.html:
Palm Tree counts 7,505 households of 5.08 people on average. Only 33.4 percent live in a home they own, owner-occupied houses carry a median value of $758,800, and median rent is $1,604 a month (Census Bureau).

  • Owner monthly cost: $2,616 with a mortgage and $1,075 without
  • Population under 18: 55.2 percent, including 18.4 percent under 5
  • Population 65 and older: 2.4 percent
  • Middle household income: $50,032 in 2024 dollars
  • Commute: 18.9 minutes on average
  • Same address as a year ago: 95.3 percent

Appraisers check how each unit is used, so keep floor plans, unit counts and rent figures handy.

Language and access shape the paperwork too. Among residents aged five and older, 92.8 percent speak a language other than English at home, and the Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures show 22.6 percent of households with a broadband subscription. If a seller or buyer prefers another language or paper copies, tell your attorney and title company at the start so the disclosure form, contract and closing statement can be explained in a way everyone follows, and so signing does not depend on email or online portals.

sections.h2: Which office records a deed for a Palm Tree property?
sections.html:
Recording happens in Goshen at the Orange County Clerk's Record Room, on the second floor of the Government Center at 255 Main Street. Documents on file there include deeds, mortgages, mortgage satisfactions, federal tax liens, judgments and lis pendens (Record Room).

  • Office computers let the public search at no cost, and an online search site is also available.
  • Copies run 65 cents a page plain (minimum $1.30) and $1.25 a page certified (minimum $5.00).
  • Your own deed costs about $5 from the clerk, and the office cautions against outside firms that bill for the same copy.
  • A free Fraud Alert sign-up sends a notice whenever a deed or mortgage is filed under your name (County Clerk).

The clerk's office also provides notary services free of charge, which helps when a deed needs an acknowledgment. Search for judgments and liens against your name before you list. A seller who finds one early can arrange the payoff, and the title search will turn it up anyway.

sections.h2: When are Palm Tree property taxes collected, and how are they challenged?
sections.html:
Orange County gives a general pattern, and the local tax collector gives the exact dates. The county's assessors page lists the periods below and tells owners to call their municipality's tax collector for a precise schedule (Orange County).

Type of tax billUsual collection period in Orange County
County and townJanuary through March
SchoolSeptember through November
VillageJune through October

Source: Orange County Assessors page.

Because Palm Tree and Kiryas Joel are the same territory, ask the tax collector which of these bills apply to your parcel. Questions about delinquent amounts and penalties go to the county finance office at 845-291-2480.

Statewide, most communities hold Grievance Day on the fourth Tuesday in May, according to the tax department, which tells owners to verify the date with their assessor (tax.ny.gov). A complaint on Form RP-524 goes to the assessor or the review board at no charge, and only the current tentative roll can be contested. Ask Palm Tree's assessor for next year's date.

sections.h2: What state transfer tax and forms apply to a Palm Tree sale?
sections.html:
The state taxes each $500 slice of the price at two dollars, with partial slices rounded up, and the seller pays unless the contract moves it (tax.ny.gov). Palm Tree's typical owned home at $758,800 rounds to a $759,000 price, which is 1,518 slices and a $3,036 tax.

Form TP-584 is the combined return. File it with the county clerk by the 15th day after the deed changes hands, with the tax. A buyer owes a further 1 percent mansion tax if the residence costs $1 million or more.

Investors should note a separate rule. If an LLC sits on either side of a deal for a building of up to four units, the return is not accepted without names and addresses of its members, managers and authorized persons, and any member that is itself a business must be traced down to individuals. Collect those details before closing day.

sections.h2: Which questions on the state form matter when a Palm Tree house is rented?
sections.html:
Before the buyer signs, the owner of a house with up to four units must supply the state's seller disclosure form (Real Property Law 462). Selling as is remains allowed, and the form is no warranty.

Question 4 asks whether anyone besides the owner has a lease, easement or other right to use or occupy any part of the property. Since only 33.4 percent of households here own their homes, buyers tend to ask about leases and rents early, so pull together copies and a rent roll. Other topics on the form include certificates of occupancy, shared walls or driveways, flood zones, water and sewage service, detectors, and the roof, heating and plumbing.

With the town and village governments merged, ask Palm Tree town hall which office issues building permits and certificates of occupancy for your street. Get the reply in writing if work was done on the house.

sections.h2: Who benefits from a cash sale in Palm Tree?
sections.html: Owners with a deadline, deferred repairs or occupied units sometimes prefer it. Without a lender, closing turns on payoff letters, title clearance and recording in Goshen. Ask for terms in writing, find out who covers each transfer cost, and have a New York lawyer review the contract.

faqs.q: Is Palm Tree simply another name for Kiryas Joel?
faqs.a: Their boundaries match. Palm Tree took over the village's territory when it separated from Monroe on January 1, 2019. A deed may name either one, so confirm which description your title company uses.

faqs.q: Where does a Palm Tree deed get recorded?
faqs.a: In Goshen, with the Orange County Clerk, whose Record Room is on the second floor of the Government Center at 255 Main Street. Owners can also enroll in the clerk's free Fraud Alert.

faqs.q: How big is the state's transfer tax bill on a $759,000 sale in Palm Tree?
faqs.a: $3,036, at two dollars per $500. The seller normally covers it. A buyer owes the 1 percent mansion tax only when a residence reaches $1 million, and the TP-584 return and payment go to the county clerk within 15 days of delivery.

faqs.q: Which months does Orange County use to collect county and town tax?
faqs.a: Mostly January to March, with school bills running September to November. The county says periods vary by municipality, so the Palm Tree tax collector has the final schedule for your bill.

faqs.q: Do tenants have to be listed on the form for a Palm Tree house?
faqs.a: In effect, yes. Question 4 asks whether anyone other than the owner has a lease or a right to use or occupy any part of the property. Answer from your own knowledge, attach extra pages if needed, and hand the form over before the contract is signed.
